universalAnswers.whatHappened: On September 9, HoneyBook announced a plugin connecting its client-management service to ChatGPT.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: HoneyBook stores client work such as projects, contracts, invoices and payments; its plugin lets ChatGPT work with selected parts of that account.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: HoneyBook supports the dated announcement, account connection, draft boundary and disconnect; OpenAI supports the product functions, resource approval and account requirement.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: Official product sources establish stated behaviour, not effectiveness, ChatGPT plan availability or behaviour of other plugins.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: An existing HoneyBook user can understand what the connection can read and prepare, and where her approval remains required.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: The change is for people who already have a HoneyBook account and choose to connect it.
universalAnswers.changesNow: Users can ask about selected HoneyBook records and prepare stated drafts through ChatGPT.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: The sources do not establish ChatGPT plan availability or tested results for every account.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Choose the HoneyBook resources the connection may reach, then review a draft before approving a change or client message.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: What account information can this connection reach, and which proposed action still waits for me?

model-tool-release.productRange: The plugin connects ChatGPT to selected resources in a HoneyBook account.
model-tool-release.newCapabilities: It can answer account-grounded questions and prepare stated items such as proposals or payment requests.
model-tool-release.bestFitTasks: Examples include checking overdue payments or project status and preparing a proposal from a saved template.
model-tool-release.notFor: The sources do not support a generic business adviser, automatic sending, or claims about other plugins.
model-tool-release.nearestAlternatives: No alternative product comparison is needed to explain this HoneyBook-specific connection.
model-tool-release.availability: The official pages present the HoneyBook plugin; a HoneyBook account is required. No ChatGPT plan claim is made.
model-tool-release.freePaidBoundary: A HoneyBook account is required; no free or paid ChatGPT tier boundary is claimed.
model-tool-release.costBoundary: No reader price is stated in this article.
model-tool-release.limitations: The plugin reaches only approved HoneyBook resources, and prepared work remains subject to review and approval.
model-tool-release.technicalExampleProportionality: One saved-template proposal example shows selected records leading to a draft and an approval decision.
model-tool-release.vendorEvidenceBoundary: HoneyBook supports its announcement and controls; OpenAI supports directory functions and the account requirement.

translation.newsVersionExact: On September 9, HoneyBook announced a plugin that connects its client-management service to ChatGPT.
translation.actualMeaningExact: The plugin can prepare work from the connected account; you remain the person who decides whether that HoneyBook change or client message happens.
translation.mechanismExact: The boundary is read, draft, review, approve.
translation.familiarExampleExact: You could ask which payments are overdue, where a project stands or have a proposal prepared from a saved template.

jargon.plainMeaning: connects its client-management service to ChatGPT

learningConnections.learningPayoff: AI Fundamentals 101 chapter 13.3 explains how a system can prepare an action while an authorised person decides whether it happens.
